summary: Iteration 5: IN-APP crypto flow (direct intent, no hosted redirect) fully validated. 16/17 backend pytest pass and both frontends (/dashboard/deposit, /pay/<slug>) reach step-3 tracker with real Tron deposit address, QR, amount and status polling. Real IzichangePay /v1/payment-intents/direct calls return valid TRC20 addresses (e.g. TUEQs6L3gUx6S7wNP4N4WZ6zG77Dj7D2gQ, TU25df5ZErQma8sJb81qUbEgxCMPirXxQ4). Webhook payment_intent.completed correctly credits balance_usdt and transitions status to confirmed/paid for both /api/deposits/crypto and /api/links/pay. Webhook security (bad sig / missing header / old timestamp / duplicate) all pass. GET /api/crypto/assets is public, returns 47+ assets, contains USDT.TRC20 with memo_required=false, and NEVER exposes sk_live_ / whsec_ keys. Frontend bundle grep + fetched main.*.js from the served URL also contain no secrets. Merchant API /api/v1/payments (hosted flow) still works and rejects invalid bearer with 401.

minor.issue: Empty refund_address ("") is ACCEPTED and returns 200 with a valid deposit address. Spec requires 422 (Pydantic validation). Root cause: models.py CryptoDepositRequest.refund_address has no min_length constraint AND server.py only does .strip() without a non-empty check. Same issue for LinkPayRequest.refund_address and probably full_name. Fix: use Field(..., min_length=1) or add explicit `if not req.refund_address.strip(): raise HTTPException(422, ...)`. Vendor unexpectedly does not reject empty refundAddress.

action_items: Add min_length=1 validation on CryptoDepositRequest.refund_address, LinkPayRequest.refund_address (and ideally full_name) so empty strings return 422 as specified. This is a real security/UX gap: an empty refund address means IzichangePay has no way to refund the customer in an edge case.
critical_code_review_comments: models.py: CryptoDepositRequest.refund_address and LinkPayRequest.refund_address are plain `str` — no min_length. Empty strings pass validation and reach IzichangePay which accepts them (200). Add Field(..., min_length=1).

server.py::create_crypto_deposit: full_name is split with maxsplit=1; single-word names produce first==last (harmless but odd). Consider a dedicated last_name field or default last='.' per IzichangePay convention.
server.py::webhook payment_intent.completed handler is idempotent per doc via unique event_id on webhook_events collection — verified via duplicate test (200 + duplicate:true). Good.

server.py sanitized error mapping (address/coin/other) is present and vendor phrasing 'Passerelle crypto: ...' is no longer surfaced from /api/deposits/crypto for direct-intent errors — confirmed via test_invalid_refund_address_format and test_unknown_asset_code_sanitized.

rca of the issue: Only issue is validation gap: CryptoDepositRequest.refund_address / LinkPayRequest.refund_address in /app/backend/models.py are plain `str` with no min_length. Server code does `req.refund_address.strip()` and forwards to IzichangePay which unexpectedly ACCEPTS empty strings, so empty refund_address returns 200 instead of the specified 422. Reproduction: POST /api/deposits/crypto with refund_address:"" and other valid fields → 200 with a valid deposit address. Fix: add Field(..., min_length=1) in models.py OR raise HTTPException(422) in server.py before calling izipay.create_direct_intent when the stripped value is empty.
